- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.67) or shows strong reversal, model often overreacts; reduce forecast sharply to avoid overshoot.  
- Model frequently overestimates prices after sharp spikes in sentiment or true outcomes; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 10–20% for 2–3 days post-spike.  
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 3+ consecutive high sentiment days); add a small upward bias to forecast to capture reversion toward historical mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven tail risks; increase forecast variance or add a 10–15% buffer for high-sentiment periods.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to be 5–10% higher than true outcome to account for delayed reaction.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 3–5 days show strong sentiment divergence from forecast, apply a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” rule to dampen model’s overconfidence.
